14448-cromwell-a-drama-in-five-acts.creator: Alfred B. Richards
14448-cromwell-a-drama-in-five-acts.description: A book by Alfred B. Richards. have I known, Since but a natural part of this was I, Whose voice is now a discord to the sounds Once daily mellow'd in my youthful being. Methinks I feel like one that long hath read A strange and chequer'd story, and doth rise, With a deep sigh to be _himself_ again.

arxiv-1706-06307.title: Diffusiophoretic manipulation of particles in a drop deposited on a hydrogel
arxiv-1706-06307.creator: François Boulogne, Sangwoo Shin, Julien Dervaux, Laurent Limat, Howard A. Stone
arxiv-1706-06307.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by François Boulogne, Sangwoo Shin, Julien Dervaux, Laurent Limat, Howard A. Stone. We report an experimental study on the manipulation of colloidal particles in a drop sitting on a hydrogel. The manipulation is achieved by diffusiophoresis, which describes a directed motion of particles induced by solute gradients. By letting the solute concentrations for the drop and the hydrogel be different, we control the motion of particles in a stable suspension, which is otherwise difficult to achieve.

arxiv-2109-15057.title: Dynamical symmetry breaking through AI: The dimer self-trapping transition
arxiv-2109-15057.creator: G. P. Tsironis, G. D. Barmparis, D. K. Campbell
arxiv-2109-15057.description: Abstract The nonlinear dimer obtained through the nonlinear Schrödinger equation has been a workhorse for the discovery the role nonlinearity plays in strongly interacting systems. While the analysis of the stationary states demonstrates the onset of a symmetry broken state for some degree of nonlinearity, the full dynamics maps the system into an effective ϕ 4 \phi^{4} model.

arxiv-2201-09118.title: Optimizing Huffman Decoding for Error-Bounded Lossy Compression on GPUs
arxiv-2201-09118.creator: Cody Rivera ⋆, Sheng Di 3, Jiannan Tian 2, Xiaodong Yu 3, Dingwen Tao 2 ⋆, Franck Cappello 3
arxiv-2201-09118.description: Abstract More and more HPC applications require fast and effective compression techniques to handle large volumes of data in storage and transmission. Not only do these applications need to compress the data effectively during simulation, but they also need to perform decompression efficiently for post hoc analysis.

arxiv-2209-14989.title: A subpolynomial-time algorithm for the free energy of one-dimensional quantum systems in the thermodynamic limit
arxiv-2209-14989.creator: Hamza Fawzi, Omar Fawzi, Samuel O. Scalet
arxiv-2209-14989.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hamza Fawzi, Omar Fawzi, Samuel O. Scalet. We introduce a classical algorithm to approximate the free energy of local, translation-invariant, one-dimensional quantum systems in the thermodynamic limit of infinite chain size. While the ground state problem (i.e., the free energy at temperature T = 0 T=0 ) for these systems is expected to be computationally hard even for quantum computers, our algorithm runs for any fixed temperature T > 0 T>0 in subpolynomial time, i.e., in time O ⁡ ( ( 1 ε )

arxiv-2210-12035.creator: João Carmona 1 2 , Tamás Karácsony 1 2 3 , João Paulo Silva Cunha 1 2
arxiv-2210-12035.description: Abstract Human motion analysis has seen drastic improvements recently, however, due to the lack of representative datasets, for clinical in-bed scenarios it is still lagging behind. To address this issue, we implemented BlanketGen, a pipeline that augments videos with synthetic blanket occlusions. With this pipeline, we generated an augmented version of the pose estimation dataset 3DPW called BlanketGen-3DPW.

arxiv-2211-00510.creator: Guo-Liang Yu 1, Yan Meng 1, Zhen-Yu Li 2, Zhi-Gang Wang 1, Lu Jie 1
arxiv-2211-00510.description: Abstract In this work, we perform a systematic study of the mass spectra, the root mean square(r.m.s.) radii and the radial density distributions of the doubly charmed baryons Ξ c ​ c \Xi_{cc} and Ω c ​ c \Omega_{cc} .

arxiv-2304-07202.title: Scalar transport and nucleation in quasi-two-dimensional starting jets and puffs Journal: International Journal of Multiphase Flow
arxiv-2304-07202.creator: You-An Lee, Detlef Lohse, Sander G. Huisman
arxiv-2304-07202.description: Abstract We experimentally investigate the early-stage scalar mixing and transport with solvent exchange in a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) jet. We inject an ethanol/oil mixture upward into quiescent water, forming quasi-2D turbulent buoyant jets and triggering the ouzo effect with initial Reynolds numbers, R ​ e 0 = 420 , Re_{0}=420, 840 , 840, and 1680 1680 .

arxiv-2308-09833.title: Achieving quantum metrological performance and exact Heisenberg limit precision through superposition of s s -spin coherent states
arxiv-2308-09833.creator: Hanan Saidi, Hanane El Hadfi, Abdallah Slaoui, Rachid Ahl Laamara
arxiv-2308-09833.description: Abstract Résumé In quantum phase estimation, the Heisenberg limit provides the ultimate accuracy over quasi-classical estimation procedures. However, realizing this limit hinges upon both the detection strategy employed for output measurements and the characteristics of the input states. This study delves into quantum phase estimation using s s -spin coherent states superposition.

arxiv-2401-01307.title: Restart uncertainty relation for monitored quantum dynamics
arxiv-2401-01307.creator: Ruoyu Yin, Qingyuan Wang, Sabine Tornow, Eli Barkai
arxiv-2401-01307.description: Abstract We introduce a new time-energy uncertainty relation within the context of restarts in monitored quantum dynamics. Previous studies have established that the mean recurrence time, which represents the time taken to return to the initial state, is quantized as an integer multiple of the sampling time, displaying pointwise discontinuous transitions at resonances.

arxiv-2403-12309.title: Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Observations via World Models
arxiv-2403-12309.creator: Armin Karamzade, Kyungmin Kim, Montek Kalsi, Roy Fox
arxiv-2403-12309.description: Abstract In standard reinforcement learning settings, agents typically assume immediate feedback about the effects of their actions after taking them. However, in practice, this assumption may not hold true due to physical constraints and can significantly impact the performance of learning algorithms. In this paper, we address observation delays in partially observable environments.

arxiv-2409-04542.title: Towards Hybrid Embedded Feature Selection and Classification Approach with Slim-TSF
arxiv-2409-04542.creator: Anli Ji, Chetraj Pandey, Berkay Aydin
arxiv-2409-04542.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anli Ji, Chetraj Pandey, Berkay Aydin. Traditional solar flare forecasting approaches have mostly relied on physics-based or data-driven models using solar magnetograms, treating flare predictions as a point-in-time classification problem. This approach has limitations, particularly in capturing the evolving nature of solar activity. Recognizing the limitations of traditional flare forecasting approaches, our research aims to uncover hidden relationships and the evolutionary characteristics of solar flares and their source regions.

arxiv-2411-09322.title: Gravitational wave asteroseismology of neutron stars with unified EOS: on the role of high-order nuclear empirical parameters
arxiv-2411-09322.creator: Guilherme Grams, César V. Flores, César H. Lenzi
arxiv-2411-09322.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guilherme Grams, César V. Flores, César H. Lenzi. We analyze the sensitivity of non-radial fluid oscillation modes and tidal deformations in neutron stars to high-order nuclear empirical parameters (NEP). In particular, we study the impact of the curvature and skewness of the symmetry energy K sym K_{\rm sym} , Q sym Q_{\rm sym} , and the skewness of the binding energy in symmetric nuclear matter Q sat Q_{\rm sat} .

arxiv-2505-15523.title: Exciton-defect interaction and optical properties from a first-principles T-matrix approach
arxiv-2505-15523.creator: Yang-hao Chan, Jonah B. Haber, Mit H. Naik, Diana Y. Qiu, Felipe H. da Jornada
arxiv-2505-15523.description: Abstract Understanding exciton-defect interactions is critical for optimizing optoelectronic and quantum information applications in many materials. However, ab initio simulations of material properties with defects are often limited to high defect density. Here, we study effects of exciton-defect interactions on optical absorption and photoluminescence spectra in monolayer MoS 2 using a first-principles T-matrix approach.

arxiv-2510-14737.title: Free-Grained Hierarchical Recognition
arxiv-2510-14737.creator: Seulki Park Zilin Wang Stella X. Yu, University of Michigan UC Berkeley {seulki,zilinwan,stellayu}@umich.edu
arxiv-2510-14737.description: Abstract Hierarchical image classification predicts labels across a semantic taxonomy, but existing methods typically assume complete, fine-grained annotations, an assumption rarely met in practice. Real-world supervision varies in granularity, influenced by image quality, annotator expertise, and task demands; a distant bird may be labeled Bird , while a close-up reveals Bald eagle .

arxiv-2512-20567.title: Classification using quantum kernels in a radial basis function network
arxiv-2512-20567.creator: E. Micklethwaite, A. Lowe
arxiv-2512-20567.description: Abstract Radial basis function (RBF) networks are expanded to incorporate quantum kernel functions enabling a new type of hybrid quantum-classical machine learning algorithm. Using this approach, synthetic examples are introduced which allow for proof of concept on interpolation and classification applications.

europmc-pmc4238058.creator: Banjade S, Rosen MK.
europmc-pmc4238058.description: Clustering of proteins into micrometer-sized structures at membranes is observed in many signaling pathways. Most models of clustering are specific to particular systems, and relationships between physical properties of the clusters and their molecular components are not well...

pmc-11550045.title: Evaluation system of vocational education construction in China based on linked TOPSIS analysis
pmc-11550045.creator: Huiping Li
pmc-11550045.description: In response to the task of vocational education reform in the new era, in order to cultivate innovative skilled talents, it is necessary to improve traditional evaluation methods to enhance their efficiency. This study proposes an evaluation model for vocational education construction that combines grey relational analysis and approximate ideal point method (TOPSIS).

pmc-11810903.title: Machine learning for the diagnosis accuracy of bipolar disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11810903.creator: Yi Pan, Pushi Wang, Bowen Xue, Yanbin Liu, Xinhua Shen, Shiliang Wang, Xing Wang
pmc-11810903.description: BackgroundDiagnosing bipolar disorder poses a challenge in clinical practice and demands a substantial time investment. With the growing utilization of artificial intelligence in mental health, researchers are endeavoring to create AI-based diagnostic models. In this context, some researchers have sought to develop machine learning models for bipolar disorder diagnosis. Nevertheless, the accuracy of these diagnoses remains a subject of controversy.

pmc-12568988.title: A dynamic biointerface in mussels mediated by a mechanoresponsive intermediate filament-based biopolymer
pmc-12568988.creator: Lucia Youssef, Jenaes Sivasundarampillai, Emily N P Prowse, E Deniz Eren, Franziska Jehle, Christopher Thibodeaux, Adam G Hendricks, Daniel J Jackson, Matthew J Harrington
pmc-12568988.description: Mussels fabricate a distinctive biointerface that bridges their non-living biopolymeric byssus (used for anchoring in seashore habitats) with their soft-living tissue. Occurring in a region known as the byssus stem root, this biointerface is at once strong, yet also capable of on-demand release under apparent neurobiological control by the mussel, but this is not well understood.

pmc-13218525.title: Perception of artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in the Nigerian healthcare sector: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13218525.creator: Obi Peter Adigwe, Godspower Onavbavba
pmc-13218525.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has significant benefits across various facets of healthcare delivery, notably in personalised pharmacotherapy and the development of targeted health interventions for specific demographic groups. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the applications of AI and machine learning (ML) from the perspectives of healthcare professionals in Nigeria.

pmc-13247532.title: Severe autoimmunity after checkpoint inhibitor therapy in a patient with autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1
pmc-13247532.creator: Alexandra Lim, Esther M Peluso, Ian A Downs, Brian H Horwich, Maria A Velez-Velez, Melissa G Lechner
pmc-13247532.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cancer therapies targeting programmed cell death protein 1 and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 enhance antitumor immunity in many cancers. Despite its efficacy, ICI therapy can trigger severe autoimmune attacks across various organ systems, termed immune-related adverse events (irAEs).

pmc-13293339.title: Identification and response to a putatively hypervirulent, carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST395 hospital outbreak in the UK
pmc-13293339.creator: Mark I. Garvey, Robert A. Moran, Ana D. Sanches Ferreira, Jean Harker, Sarah Wilkes, Elisabeth Holden, Alan McNally
pmc-13293339.description: Here, we describe a putatively hypervirulent, carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (hv-CRKP) outbreak. Nanopore sequencing guided the infection prevention and control (IPC) responses during the outbreak. Twelve patients were identified as either being colonized and/or having clinical infections with the putative hv-CRKP, with an all-cause mortality within 6 months of 36%.

pmc-13341568.title: Feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of mindfulness-based stress reduction program on patients with nocturnal hypertension: a pilot randomized controlled trial
pmc-13341568.creator: Shuqi Wang, Sze Nok Ng, Regina Wing Shan Sit, Chapman Cheuk Tung Ying, Shuk Yun Leung, Jinghao Han, Yue Kwan Choi, Kam Fai Chow, Wai Ho Chung, Benjamin Hon Kei Yip, Richard J. McManus, Samuel Yeung Shan Wong, Eric Kam Pui Lee
pmc-13341568.description: BackgroundNocturnal blood pressure (BP) during sleep is a stronger predictor of cardiovascular events than daytime BP. This pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed to assess feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) in managing nocturnal hypertension.MethodsEligible patients were randomized to either a generic MBSR program or usual care (1:1).

pmc-13529649.title: Particulate matter 2.5 induced inflammatory responses and metabolic alterations in human monocytes
pmc-13529649.creator: Naunpun Sangphech, Tassanee Chetwittayachan, Ganjana Lertmemongkolchai, Ian Mudway, Sakchai Laksee, Jomkhwan Meerak, Pongphan Pongpanitanont, Tanapat Palaga
pmc-13529649.description: Fine particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5) is linked to rising cases of respiratory, cardiovascular, and immune-mediated diseases and increased hospitalizations in non-respiratory patients. Chiang Mai Province in Northern Thailand, faces seasonal severe PM2.5 pollution, but its impact on immune responses in human remains poorly characterized.

pmc-13571125.creator: Mohamed A Hammad, Hossam M Ashour

In the previous issue of Molecular Therapy Oncology, the study by Jian and colleagues addresses this gap by developing an artificial intelligence model (AIM) that integrates multi-omics data with advanced machine learning algorithms to predict prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity in LGG patients.

pmc-13613010.title: Chronic Methamphetamine Administration Increases Mitochondrial Density and Impairs Mitochondrial Function in the Substantia Nigra Pars Compacta
pmc-13613010.creator: Aishwarya Bhowmik, Jennifer A. Wilking, Duha Alshareef, Colin Campbell, Steven M. Graves
pmc-13613010.description: Methamphetamine (meth) is an addictive psychostimulant that induces monoamine oxidase (MAO)‐dependent mitochondrial oxidative stress and MAO‐dependent degeneration of substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) dopamine neurons in male mice, suggesting that meth‐induced mitochondrial oxidative stress is necessary for degeneration. However, the impact of chronic in vivo meth administration on SNc mitochondria is unclear.
